trial_court: Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) Sirsi, MC No.29/2006 and M.C No.8/2007

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Suvarna Kom Ratnakar Shet, wife, Bank Employee
parties.respondent_defendant: Ratnakar Vinayak Shet, husband, Bank Employee

facts_of_case: The wife filed a petition for divorce and judicial separation in MC No.29/2006, which was allowed by the trial court. She also filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights in M.C No.8/2007, which was dismissed by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: Desertion is a matter of inference to be drawn from the facts and circumstances of each case.
legal_principles.held: The inference may be drawn from certain facts which may not in another case be capable of leading to the same inference.
cited_cases: BWIN CHANDER JAISINGHBHAT SHAll VS. PRABHAWATI (AIR 1957 SC 176)

legal_principles.principle: The offence of desertion commences when the fact of separation and the animus deserendi co-exist.
legal_principles.held: The de facto separation may have commenced without the necessary animus or it may be that the separation and the animus deserendi coincide in point of time.
cited_cases: BWIN CHANDER JAISINGHBHAT SHAll VS. PRABHAWATI (AIR 1957 SC 176)

legal_principles.principle: The period of desertion is not necessarily continuous; it can be interrupted by a bonafide offer to resume cohabitation.
legal_principles.held: If the deserted spouse unreasonably refuses the offer, the latter may be in desertion and not the former.
cited_cases: BWIN CHANDER JAISINGHBHAT SHAll VS. PRABHAWATI (AIR 1957 SC 176)

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court are set aside.
